utterances.text: Are you suggesting, then, that we would mark them for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm suggesting at this moment they be marked for identification pending my learned friend's speedy response as to the authenticity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the Chamber will do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry. Just one thing I'd like to add. I think we may encounter a problem. We did get the list of documents, and I have prepared my cross-examination on the basis of this definitive list I got. But on this definitive list, I have three intercepts and I don't have six. That's the first point I would like to make. Second, prior to that, I got another list and I did prepare my cross-examination on the basis of this list, and I thought I had the definitive list yesterday. I listened to the Defence counsel yesterday and I understand, but we can't allow all and everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is the position. We'll mark these documents for identification. Counsel will transmit them to you after the hearing. We'll have to investigate independently whether you were, in fact, served with the documents. If we find that you were not served and you are in any way embarrassed in your preparation for cross-examination, we'll take that into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can I deal with these orally now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The first being -- the first being an intercept dated 15 June 1995, PT 2438.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mark them separately, individually, for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as Exhibit P37.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I note that our case manager Ms. Bosnjakovic will be supplying my learned friend with the audio files to go with these transcripts that we're dealing with at this moment immediately after the close of proceedings today so that the audio files can be assigned related numbers - I would suggest 37A for the audio file or 37B - so that the numbers are cross-referenced. Oh, I see that my court officer -- that the court officer already has these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The next, which is a document, PT 2430.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be marked for identification as Exhibit P38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That being a contextual document, an order to all Sarajevo-Romanija Corps units to prepare for a Muslim offensive out of Sarajevo. The next one bears the number P595.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification as P39.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That being an intercepted conversation between Dragomir Milosevic and Ratko Mladic, dated 16 June 1995. The next -- pardon me with my pen. The next one being PT 2446.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification as P40.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your indulgence for one moment, Your Honour, so I can group these all together. The next one bears the number PT 2488.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification as P41.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That being an intercepted telephone conversation between one Prstojevic and one Veselinovic. The following one is PT 2493.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification as P42.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That being a document drafted by -- or signed by Dragomir Milosevic, setting out conditions on the Sarajevo front, mentioning an artillery salvo hit the TV building. And, again, your very brief indulgences, Your Honours. I think that covers those contextual documents, Your Honour, and I would just like now to go back to documents which Lieutenant-Colonel Fortin has specifically prepared himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The first one bears the number PT 2472. Lieutenant-Colonel, could you please confirm that you were the drafter of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think it's a two-page document, and you'll have to take us to the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I drafted that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could it bear the next exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P43.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With your indulgence, Your Honours, I propose to spend the next five minutes with the last two documents, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The next one, bearing the number P2473. If you could scroll down and go to the next page after that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel, is this another record of a meeting prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: LOUIS FORTIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could it receive the next exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P44.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the next document is PT 2479, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel - if we could scroll down again and go to the last page - another document prepared by you, a record of a meeting between General Smith and Colonel Meille. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LOUIS FORTIN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If that could receive the next exhibit number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P45.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes the 92 ter examination, keeping your guidance in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are at the end of the day's proceedings now. Ms. Isailovic, you should take advantage of the evening and tomorrow morning to examine these documents that you have not seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly turn your microphone on, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I just wanted to thank you and I shall do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll adjourn until tomorrow, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of January, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.,
